### Summary

This section keeps the selector and the guard of the radial velocity correction. The covariance identity and the
finite-difference form are derived in @sec-ch04-x1masscov and are not repeated here. At the pin the selector is the
deck key `dynamics/x1-mass-covariance`, default false. Like `flux-covariance`, the schema requires every block of a
run to make the same choice.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Selects the radial mean conversion of @eq-ch04-x1masscov-gap.

**Data.** Density and radial velocity in; corrected reconstruction velocity out.

**Placement.** Well-balanced radial branch, before reconstruction; input restored afterwards.

**Activation.** `dynamics/x1-mass-covariance: true`; the default is `false`.

**Guarantee / limits.** With radial gravity, at least three $x_1$ cells per block are required.

**Evidence.** Tests below, @tbl-ch12-mass-covariance-tests; solver ctests were not run.
:::

Local symbols: $\rho$ is density [$\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$], radial velocity has units [m s$^{-1}$], and $\Delta x_1$
is cell width [m].

### Derivation

See @sec-ch04-x1masscov for the mean-conversion identity. The chapter's check line `[C4]` re-derives the
mass-weighted mean with rational polynomial integration, together with the lateral covariance identity it shares
the derivation with [check `src/snapy_report/ch12/checks/configuration_check.py`, output
`src/snapy_report/ch12/checks/configuration_check.out`].

### Numerical method

`HydroImpl::x1_mass_covariance` ({{< code src/hydro/hydro.hpp HydroImpl::x1_mass_covariance >}}) returns the
block's option. With nonzero $g_1$, `HydroImpl::reset` ({{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::reset >}}) refuses
fewer than three $x_1$ cells, because the one-sided wall slope spans three cells. `HydroImpl::forward`
({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}) hands the option to the well-balanced $x_1$
reconstruction. In `WellBalancedX1::forward` ({{< code src/recon/well_balanced_x1.cpp WellBalancedX1::forward >}})
the correction proceeds in five steps:

1. It forms centred density and velocity slopes with `x1_cov_d1_centred`
   ({{< code src/hydro/x1_mass_covariance.hpp x1_cov_d1_centred >}}), using the three-point form on a stretched grid.
2. At a physical non-outflow wall it replaces the density slope in the first and last cell with a one-sided
   second-order slope (`x1_cov_one_sided`, {{< code src/hydro/x1_mass_covariance.hpp x1_cov_one_sided >}}).
3. It subtracts the covariance term from the radial velocity.
4. It gives the corrected velocity odd ghosts at those walls.
5. It reconstructs, and restores the input velocity afterwards.

The correction is part of each explicit hydro call. It adds no implicit matrix term.

```{python}

#| fig-alt: "rho-weighted velocity; centered slopes; wall: three owned cells; subtract covariance; reconstruct and restore."
#| echo: false
```

### Code

**How to use it.** Set `x1-mass-covariance: true` in the `dynamics` block, and give each block at least three $x_1$
cells. The guard acts with radial gravity, as in this fragment of a complete input card:

```yaml
forcing:
  const-gravity:
    grav1: -9.8     # m s^-2
    gravity-work: face
```

For two $x_1$ cells with radial gravity, reset refuses the stencil with "dynamics/x1-mass-covariance needs at least
3 x1 cells per block, got 2; set it to false".

`WellBalancedX1::forward` ({{< code src/recon/well_balanced_x1.cpp WellBalancedX1::forward >}}) contains this
correction step:

```cpp
    wx1[IVX] -= dx1f * dx1f / 12. * rho_1 * w_1 / density;
```

Here `dx1f` is the radial cell width [m], `rho_1` the density slope [$\mathrm{kg\,m^{-4}}$], and `w_1` the radial
velocity slope [$\mathrm{s^{-1}}$]. Dividing their product by density gives the velocity correction [m s$^{-1}$] of
@eq-ch04-x1masscov-gap, whose linear identity is checked by `[C4]`.

: Implementation sites for the mass-covariance selector. {#tbl-ch12-mass-covariance-code}

1. Read the key per block. The anchor `x1_mass_covariance` is in
   {{< code src/hydro/hydro.hpp HydroImpl::x1_mass_covariance >}}.
2. At setup with gravity, refuse fewer than three $x_1$ cells. The anchor `nx1` is in
   {{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::reset >}}.
3. In the well-balanced branch, correct the velocity, reconstruct, and restore. The anchor `rho_1` is in
   {{< code src/recon/well_balanced_x1.cpp WellBalancedX1::forward >}}.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
The interior, wall, seam, CUDA, MPI and combined-key accuracy of this correction is unmeasured here. The registered
evidence is the setup guard and the perturbation-flux arm, whose tolerances were not re-read for this edit. The
Cartesian coefficient does not establish exactness on a curved measure.

The complete switch inventory is @sec-ch12-matrix.
:::
